newsitem.title: UK: Commercial Union up on French acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union up on French acquisition.

text.p: Shares in Commercial Union Plc moved ahead briskly on Friday morning as the market reacted to its acquisition of a French life assurer, dealers said.
CU shares were up 14 pence, or 2.13 percent, to 668.5p by 0745 GMT, in volume of 1.2 million,while the FTSE-100 index was 8.0 points, or 0.18 percent, lower at 4,380.5.
Marketmakers said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett had put a buy note out on CU this morning.
"I understand they (ABN) recommend buying all the way up to seven pounds after the French deal," a dealer at a British bank said.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett was not immediately available.
Composite insurer Commercial Union upped its share of the French life market to around 4.5 percent on Thursday.

It bought 73.1 percent of SEV (Societe d'Epargne Viagere), a French life assurer, and 100 percent of a French insurance broking business, which distributes products of life insurance organisation AFER (Association Francaise d'Epargne et de Retraite) products, from Compagnie de Suez.
Commercial Union already owned 1.9 percent of SEV.
Separately, Lehman Brothers put out an 'underperform' note saying the acquisition did little in the short term but added that the move was "of long-term merit".
